sampling_model.design: Two independent samples from one population: \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) and \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\ge1\) labeled records and \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records with \(X\in[d]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed known constant satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\); no minimum \(p_x\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Neither \(p_x\), \(e_x\), nor \(\mu_{ax}\) is known. The estimator handle uses labeled outcome marks and pooled treatment--mass factorial moments with separate information budgets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the supervised lower scale \(n^{-1}+d^2/(n^2\log^2 n)\), and Theorem 5 shows that knowing \(P_X\) alone can leave constant minimax risk.
The paper gives robust and locally efficient semi-supervised ATE estimation using a small chart-reviewed sample and a much larger EHR cohort.
Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1 give an asymptotic expansion and root-\(n\) normality under explicit nuisance-error controls in the labeled--unlabeled experiment.
The two-sample results derive regular efficient influence functions and an attaining asymptotically normal estimator under support and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs minimax estimators by applying factorial-moment polynomial estimation on rare cells and a bias-corrected plug-in rule on regular cells.
Theorem 1 matches entropy upper and lower rates through best polynomial approximation and its moment-matching dual.

body.tldr: Gold-standard outcomes may be available only for \(n\) chart-reviewed records even though treatment and baseline covariates are available for another \(m\) records. The research kernel is the sharp finite-sample minimax MSE over every \((n,m,d)\) regime, delivered through three open questions: a mixed marked--unmarked polynomial upper bound, an exactly common-\(P_{XA}\) converse, and their matched annotation frontier. A finite \(d=2\), \(\epsilon=1/4\) calculation shows a statistic multiplying a labeled outcome mark by an independent marginal factor and two hypotheses with identical auxiliary laws but different ATEs. The frontier must recover the catalogued supervised rate only as its \(m=0\) endpoint, prove convergence to the explicitly defined known-\(P_{XA}\) risk for each fixed \((n,d)\) as \(m\to\infty\), and give explicit necessary and sufficient thresholds for consistency, root-\(n\) MSE, and strict order improvement.

project_justification.gap: Supervised discrete ATE theory identifies a logarithmic rare-cell barrier, whereas semi-supervised causal papers establish regular local efficiency under nuisance consistency or working models. Neither literature quantifies the joint finite-sample experiment in which outcome-bearing information has size \(n\) and treatment--mass information has size \(n+m\), with null cells and unrestricted regression functions; the standard adjustment identity and Blackwell monotonicity do not answer that quantitative question.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an annotation frontier that is uniform in \(n,m,d\), respects the different information budgets inside each polynomial monomial, and uses lower priors invisible to every auxiliary observation rather than recycling a supervised prior.
project_justification.fill: The three focal open questions seek a total mixed-factorial heavy--light estimator, an exactly common-\(P_{XA}\) fuzzy-hypothesis converse, and one matching numerical rate. The rate must reproduce the catalogued supervised formula at \(m=0\), converge to the formally defined known-\(P_{XA}\) risk for fixed \((n,d)\), and yield explicit necessary and sufficient inequalities in \(n,m_n,d_n\) for consistency, parametric MSE, and strict order improvement.

body.related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024}, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, derive the supervised moment-matching obstruction; their Theorem 5 and Appendix C.9 show why knowledge of \(P_X\) does not reveal the propensity. The matched supervised rate is recorded in the in-catalogue result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) and enters only as the required \(m=0\) endpoint, not as a solve target or contribution. Cheng, Ananthakrishnan, and Cai, \cite{ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021}, Sections 2.1 and 4, supply the chart-review motivation and a robust locally efficient estimator that leverages outcome surrogates; the present target is only a baseline discrete benchmark and does not claim their surrogate efficiency. Chakrabortty and Dai, \cite{ChakraborttyDai2024}, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, derive a two-sample expansion whose root-\(n\) conclusion depends on propensity and regression error rates. Kato, \cite{Kato2025}, Theorems 4.2 and 4.4, gives the adjacent regular two-stratum efficiency theory under fixed sample fractions and nuisance conditions. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, Sections I-A and III, motivate the rare-cell polynomial versus smooth-cell split and coefficient-sensitive factorial analysis. Wu and Yang, \cite{WuYang2016}, Theorem 1 and Appendix E, supply the best-approximation and moment-matching duality used to enforce the new common-marginal converse. The finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) separates these roles concretely: its mixed statistic uses an outcome mark from \(\mathcal L_1\) and a marginal factor from \(\mathcal U_1\), while its two hypotheses agree exactly on every auxiliary observation. None of these sources states an all-regime minimax rate for the present unequal-information ATE experiment or the fixed-\((n,d)\) convergence of its risk to the known-\(P_{XA}\) experiment.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) is diagnostic rather than a rate theorem. Its mixed statistic has expectation \(2q_{11}p_1=1/4\) in the displayed law, so the approximation bias is visible against the treated-cell target \(1/2\); the full hybrid must choose a higher degree and control its tails. Its two common-\(P_{XA}\) point masses have labeled total variation \(1-(3/4)^n\), so a moment-matched fuzzy refinement is required for a sharp lower bound. Neither mechanism follows by replacing \(n\) with \(n+m\) in a supervised construction: that substitution would estimate \(q_{ax}\), an outcome-marked mass, from records without \(Y\), and a supervised prior that changes \(P_{XA}\) becomes distinguishable as \(m\) grows. The presolve candidate \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{(n+m)\log(en)\}]^2\}\) remains diagnostic evidence only because the false-light tail bound, branch-mean variance, normalization of the common-marginal lower prior, and fixed-sample transfers are unproved.
body.honest_scope: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and occupied-cell overlap, the standard setup identity is \(E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=\tau(P)=\sum_{x=1}^{d}p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\), including null cells. As an unnumbered Blackwell sanity check, \(R_\epsilon(n,m+1,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\) and \(R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,0,d)\). The matched supervised rate from \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) is solely the required \(m=0\) reduction. The known-marginal benchmark means the experiment that supplies the exact table \(P_{XA}\) as deterministic side information, and the only limit asserted for it is the open fixed-\((n,d)\) claim \(\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\); no triangular-array version is presumed. The exact finite-\(m\) rate, its explicit strict-separation threshold, the uniform hybrid-risk lemma, and the auxiliary-invariant lower-bound transfer are open. The project assumes neither smoothness, sparsity, effect homogeneity, outcome surrogacy, a minimum cell mass, nor selected enrollment. It does not provide confidence intervals, optimize nonuniform validation probabilities, or validate the ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 empirical data under this unrestricted model.
